terminals.name: reset filter

terminals.name: signal in
terminals.description: signal in is the waveform to be filtered.

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: FIR filter specifications
terminals.description: FIR filter specifications are the minimum values needed to specify the FIR filter.

terminals.name: Type
terminals.description: Type specifies the passband of the filter according to the following values.

terminals.name: #Taps
terminals.description: #Taps is the number of taps in the FIR filter. The default is 50.

terminals.name: Lower PB
terminals.description: Lower PB is the lower of the two passband frequencies. The default is 100 Hz.

terminals.name: Upper PB
terminals.description: Upper PB is the higher of the two passband frequencies. The default is 0.

terminals.name: Lower SB
terminals.description: Lower SB is the lower of the two stopband frequencies. The default is 200 Hz.

terminals.name: Upper SB
terminals.description: Upper SB is the higher of the two stopband frequencies. The default is 0.

terminals.name: optional FIR filter specifications
terminals.description: optional FIR filter specifications is a cluster of additional parameters that can be used when specifying an FIR filter.

terminals.name: SB Gain
terminals.description: SB Gain is the gain at the stopband frequencies. Gain may be specified in linear terms or dB. The default is –60dB.

terminals.name: Scale
terminals.description: Scale determines how the PB Gain and SB Gain parameters are interpreted.

terminals.name: Window
terminals.description: Window controls which smoothing window is applied to the truncated coefficients.

terminals.name: signal out
terminals.description: signal out is the filtered waveform.

terminals.name: filter information
terminals.description: filter information contains the magnitude and phase responses of the filter in a cluster that is ready to graph. filter information also contains the order of the filter.

terminals.name: df
terminals.description: df is the spacing between elements of the magnitude response in hertz.

terminals.name: Mag H(w)
terminals.description: Mag H(w) is an array of values containing the magnitude response of the filter.

terminals.name: phase H(w)
terminals.description: phase H(w) is the phase response of the filter.

terminals.name: df

terminals.name: Phase H(w)
terminals.description: Phase H(w) is an array of values containing the phase response of the filter, expressed in degrees.

terminals.name: order
terminals.description: order is the order of the filter.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

terminals.name: reset filter
terminals.description: reset filter forces the filter coefficients to be redesigned and the internal filter states to be reset to zero when it is TRUE.

terminals.name: signal in
terminals.description: signal in is the waveform data you want to filter for channel 1.

terminals.name: filter structure option
terminals.description: filter structure option specifies the order of the IIR cascade filter.

terminals.name: error in (no error)
terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

terminals.name: IIR filter specifications
terminals.description: IIR filter specifications is the cluster containing design parameters for an IIR filter.

terminals.name: Type
terminals.description: Type specifies the passband of the filter according to the following values.

terminals.name: Order
terminals.description: Order is the filter order.

terminals.name: Lower Fc
terminals.description: Lower Fc is the low cutoff frequency and must observe the Nyquist criterion.

terminals.name: Upper Fc
terminals.description: Upper Fc is the high cutoff frequency. This parameter is ignored when Type is 0 (lowpass) or 1 (highpass).

terminals.name: PB Ripple
terminals.description: PB Ripple must be greater than zero, and you must express it in decibels. If PB Ripple is less than or equal to zero, the VI sets the signal out waveform to be empty and returns an error. The default is 1.0.

terminals.name: SB Attenuation
terminals.description: SB Attenuation specifies the stopband attenuation. SB Attenuation must be greater than zero and expressed in decibels. If SB Attenuation is less than or equal to zero, the VI sets the signal output to zero or an empty array and returns an error. The default is 60.0.

terminals.name: optional IIR filter specifications
terminals.description: optional IIR filter specifications is a cluster containing information necessary to compute the order of an IIR filter.

terminals.name: Upper PB
terminals.description: Upper PB is the higher of the two passband frequencies. The default is 0.

terminals.name: Lower SB
terminals.description: Lower SB is the lower of the two stopband frequencies. The default is 200 Hz.

terminals.name: Upper SB
terminals.description: Upper SB is the higher of the two stopband frequencies. The default is 0.

terminals.name: PB Gain
terminals.description: PB Gain is the gain at the passband frequencies. Gain may be specified in linear terms or dB. The default is –3dB.

terminals.name: SB Gain
terminals.description: SB Gain is the gain at the stopband frequencies. Gain may be specified in linear terms or dB. The default is –60dB.

terminals.name: Scale
terminals.description: Scale determines how the Passband and Stopband gain parameters are interpreted.

terminals.name: signal out
terminals.description: signal out is the generated waveform.

terminals.name: filter information
terminals.description: filter information contains the magnitude and phase responses of the filter in a cluster that is ready to graph. filter information also contains the order of the filter.

terminals.name: df
terminals.description: df is the spacing between elements of the magnitude response in hertz.

terminals.name: Mag H(w)
terminals.description: Mag H(w) is an array of values containing the magnitude response of the filter.

terminals.name: phase H(w)
terminals.description: phase H(w) is the phase response of the filter.

terminals.name: df
terminals.description: df is the spacing between elements of the magnitude response in hertz.

terminals.name: Phase H(w)
terminals.description: Phase H(w) is an array of values containing the phase response of the filter, expressed in degrees.

terminals.name: order
terminals.description: order is the order of the filter.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

terminals.name: filter type

terminals.description: Functions 4676 ni.com sampling freq: fs is the frequency in Hz at which you want to sample X and must be greater than 0. The default is 1.0 Hz. If sampling freq: fs is less than or equal to 0, this VI sets Filtered X to an empty array and returns an error.

terminals.name: high cutoff freq: fh
terminals.description: high cutoff freq: fh is the high cutoff frequency in Hz. The default is 0.45 Hz. The VI ignores this parameter when filter type is 0 (Lowpass) or 1 (Highpass). terminals.name: low cutoff freq: fl
terminals.description: low cutoff freq: fl is the low cutoff frequency in Hz and must observe the Nyquist criterion. The default is 0.125 Hz.
